newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics falls, pressure may persist.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics falls, pressure may persist.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp shares fell Monday after rival Rockwell International Corp said it will ship its high-speed modem chips earlier than expected, and analysts said the pressure on the stock may persist.
"It would appear (Rockwell chips) are available sooner than we expected," said Rakesh Sood, an analyst for Hambrecht & Quist.
"Our view is (U.S. Robotics stock) will continue somewhat under pressure until the rollout of modems into the channel and ISPs (Internet Service Providers) are upgrading," he said.
But some analysts, including Sood, said U.S. Robotics seems to still have the advantage in the high-speed modem war.

Rockwell, for example, said it expects the first modems using its K56 chip will be available in retail stores in March, while U.S. Robotics is currently preparing to ship its first modems. And U.S. Robotics products can be immediately upgraded with software.

"I see this as a short-term weakness due to some uncertainty or confusion in the overall market place that is actually just creating a buying opportunity in U.S. Robotics stock," said John Grangaard, an analyst for GS2 Securities.
U.S. Robotics said it plans to ship both desktop modems and network hubs using its x2 technology this month.

To date, the U.S. Robotics and Rockwell have not worked out standards for the technology, which allows for information to be downloaded using conventional telephone lines at speeds of up to 56 kilobits per second.
Shares of U.S. Robotics fell 2-15/16 to 65-9/16.
